title: Deep Learning Fundamentals
blurb: The mechanics of neural networks before transformers entered the building. Backprop, optimization, the architectures that came before — and the early generative ideas that still echo in 2026.

nodes.label: Neural nets as computational graphs
nodes.description: A neural network is a graph of differentiable operations. This mental model — not 'neurons' — is what carries you all the way to transformers.
nodes.doneWhen: You can draw the forward and backward computational graph of a 2-layer MLP and a 1-D conv.

nodes.label: Backpropagation
nodes.description: The chain rule applied at scale. Implement it once by hand on a tiny example so it stops feeling like magic.
nodes.doneWhen: You can implement a 2-layer net's forward and backward pass from scratch in NumPy.

nodes.label: Optimizers (SGD, momentum, Adam) & lr schedules
nodes.description: Plain SGD, momentum, Nesterov, Adam, AdamW, learning-rate schedules (cosine, warmup, linear decay). The choices that decide whether a model trains at all.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick an optimizer and lr schedule for a new model and defend the choice.

nodes.label: Initialization & normalization
nodes.description: Xavier / He initialization, batch norm, layer norm, RMS norm. Why a model that won't train is usually a normalization-or-init problem.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why layer norm replaced batch norm in transformers.

nodes.label: Activations & loss functions
nodes.description: ReLU, GELU, SwiGLU, sigmoid, softmax; MSE, cross-entropy, contrastive losses. Which one to use and when.
nodes.doneWhen: You can match an activation and loss to a task type without thinking.

nodes.label: Convolutional neural networks
nodes.description: Conv, pooling, the standard CNN architectures (ResNet, EfficientNet). Even in 2026, CNNs win on edge vision and inside multi-modal stacks.
nodes.doneWhen: You can train a small CNN on CIFAR-10 and explain its receptive field.

nodes.label: RNNs & LSTMs (historical)
nodes.description: How sequences were modeled before attention. Mostly historical now, but the vocabulary still shows up. Skim, don't dwell.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain in one sentence why transformers replaced RNNs for long sequences.

nodes.label: Embeddings & representation learning
nodes.description: Words, tokens, items, users — all as vectors in a learned space. word2vec, fastText, sentence embeddings. The bridge to retrieval and RAG.
nodes.doneWhen: You can compute cosine similarity between sentence embeddings and reason about the geometry.

nodes.label: Attention (the pre-transformer history)
nodes.description: Bahdanau attention, Luong attention, the seq2seq with attention era. Useful context for understanding why the transformer was a leap.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe what 'attention' added to seq2seq before the transformer paper.

nodes.label: Generative models (overview)
nodes.description: Autoencoders, VAEs, GANs, diffusion. An overview, not a deep dive — enough to recognize them and connect them to the LLM-and-multimodal world that follows.
nodes.doneWhen: You can sketch the training objective of each family in one sentence.
